chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, who said:
I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a slave who caught game while he was in ihram: is there anything of the fidyah upon his master? He said: No, there is nothing upon his master.

So it does not contradict the first report, because the proper way regarding it is that we understand it to mean that if he entered ihram without his master's permission, then whenever the matter is like that, there is nothing upon his master.

key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the earlier report with which this narration is being reconciled
key_terms.الْفِدَاءِ: the compensatory penalty due for a violation
key_terms.صَيْدًا: game animal hunted while in ihram
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master, the owner of the slave
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: If a slave hunts game while in ihram, is the fidyah upon his master?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of a slave who hunts game while in ihram and whether the fidyah falls upon his master. The text states that the master bears nothing, and reconciles this with another report by interpreting it as applying to the case where the slave entered ihram without his master's permission.
